units.source_text: 明石女御也迁住二条院，与源氏共同看护紫夫人。

en.t: The Akashi Consort also moved into the Nijo residence and helped Genji care for Lady Murasaki.

units.source_text: 紫夫人对她说道：“你身上有孕，我这里恐有鬼怪，于你不利，你快快回宫去吧。”

en.t: Lady Murasaki said to her, "You are with child, and I fear there may be spirits here, which would not be good for you. Please hurry back to the palace."

units.source_text: 她看见幼小的公主长得美丽可爱，不觉泪如雨下，说道：“我不能看见她长大了！

en.t: Seeing how beautiful and lovely the little princess had become, she could not help shedding tears like rain and said, "I will not be able to see her grow up!

units.source_text: 她将来也记不起我了吧。”

en.t: In time, she will probably not remember me at all."

units.source_text: 女御听了也很伤心，眼泪流个不住。

en.t: The Consort was deeply saddened to hear this, and her tears would not stop flowing.

units.source_text: 源氏说道：“不要有这种不祥的想法！

en.t: Genji said, "You must not think such ominous thoughts!

units.source_text: 你的病虽然重，但是决无危险。

en.t: Although your illness is serious, there is certainly no danger.

units.source_text: 人生穷通夭寿，都是由心决定的。

en.t: A person's fortune or hardship, and even a short or long life, are all determined by the heart.

units.source_text: 心胸宽大的人，幸福亦随之而增多；心境狭隘的人，即使有缘身登高位，生涯也不得丰裕。

en.t: For those with generous hearts, happiness increases accordingly; for those with narrow minds, even if fate raises them to high rank, their lives will not be rich or fulfilled.

units.source_text: 性情急躁的人，往往寿命不长；心神旷达的人，长寿之例甚多。”

en.t: People of impatient temperament often do not live long; among those with broad and open spirits, there are many examples of long life."

units.source_text: 便向神佛祷告，说明紫夫人性情何等温良，在世并无罪孽，乞赐早日痊愈。

en.t: He then prayed to the gods and Buddhas, declaring how gentle and good Lady Murasaki was, how she had committed no sins in this world, and begging that she be granted a swift recovery.

units.source_text: 执行祈祷的阿阇梨、守夜僧人，以及一切准许近侍的高僧，闻知源氏如此忧惧惶惑，大家深感同情，祈祷更加诚恳了。

en.t: The acaryas performing the rites, the monks keeping vigil through the night, and all the eminent priests permitted to attend nearby heard of Genji's fear, grief, and bewilderment; deeply moved with sympathy, they prayed even more earnestly.

units.source_text: 紫夫人有时病情略见好转，但五六日之后又重起来。

en.t: At times Lady Murasaki's condition seemed to improve a little, but after five or six days it would worsen again.

units.source_text: 缠绵病榻，几经日月，一直不肯痊愈。

en.t: She remained confined to her sickbed for days and months, never fully recovering.

units.source_text: 源氏觉得这病状不妙，难道真个没有希望了？

en.t: Genji felt that the illness was taking a bad turn and wondered whether there truly was no hope.

units.source_text: 心中十分悲伤。

en.t: His heart was filled with deep sorrow.

units.source_text: 生怕有鬼怪作祟，然而并无明显迹象。

en.t: He was terribly afraid that some spirit might be causing harm, yet there was no clear sign of it.

units.source_text: 病苦究竟何在？

en.t: Where, after all, did the suffering of the illness lie?

units.source_text: 却也说不出来，只见病体日复一日地衰弱下去。

en.t: No one could say; they could only see her sick body weakening day by day.

units.source_text: 因此源氏更觉悲伤不堪，心情片刻也没有安宁的时候了。

en.t: Because of this, Genji felt even more overcome with grief, and his heart had not a moment of peace.
